title: Compact isomorphism tests imply preservation by a right adjoint
statement: Let C and D be preadditive categories [def-weil-additive-category] with universe-u coproducts, and assume D is locally u-small [def-weil-size-convention]. Let R:C→D and c:D→C be adjoint, R left and c right, meaning Hom_D(R(A),B) is naturally isomorphic to Hom_C(A,c(B)). Let S be a universe-u set and G:S→C such that G_s and R(G_s) are compact [def-pc-compact-object] for every s. Assume that for every g:A→B in C, bijectivity of postcomposition Hom_C(G_s,A)→Hom_C(G_s,B) for every s implies that g is an isomorphism. Then c preserves every existing set-indexed coproduct, in every indexing universe.

source.place: Tag 0A9R, adjunction Hom calculation; generalized to preadditive categories with explicit isomorphism tests

proof.text: Initial objects supplied by empty coproducts are zero objects in preadditive categories. Each adjoint is additive: the left adjoint preserves finite coproducts, the right preserves finite products, and both finite shapes are biproducts.

For K indexed by Type u form the canonical comparison ⊕c(K_i)→c(⊕K_i). For each s, compactness of G_s and R(G_s), with the additive Hom equivalence of the adjunction between them, makes postcomposition by this comparison a bijection. Check the identity on each direct-sum summand: adjunction naturality carries composition with a coprojection to composition with its c-image, exactly the definition of the comparison. The detection assumption makes the comparison invertible, which is equivalent to preservation of the discrete colimit.

For any larger family with an existing coproduct B in D, its nonzero indices inject into End(B). For each i, the coproduct universal property gives π_i:B→K_i equal to the identity after the i-th coprojection and zero after the others. The idempotent ι_iπ_i is nonzero if K_i is nonzero, and is distinct from ι_jπ_j for i≠j, as is seen by precomposition with ι_i and postcomposition with π_i. Local u-smallness of D makes the nonzero support u-small. Shrink this support to Type u and delete the zero summands. The universal property identifies its coproduct with B. The right adjoint c preserves zero objects because they are terminal, so the same deletion applies to the image family. Apply the Type u case and undo the reindexing and zero insertions. The empty family is included.

mathlib_searches.query: A small family of compact objects detecting isomorphisms and sent to compact objects by a left adjoint makes the right adjoint preserve coproducts
A right adjoint preserves arbitrary coproducts if its left adjoint sends compact generators to compact objects

theorem compactTests_rightAdjoint_preservesCoproducts
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{wC} C] [Preadditive C] [HasCoproducts.{u} C]
    {D : Type uD} [Category.{wD} D] [Preadditive D] [HasCoproducts.{u} D]
    [LocallySmall.{u} D]
    (R : C ⥤ D) (c : D ⥤ C) (adj : R ⊣ c)
    (S : Type u) (G : S → C)
    (hcompact : ∀ s, IsCompactObject (G s) ∧ IsCompactObject (R.obj (G s)))
    (hdetect : ∀ (A B : C) (g : A ⟶ B),
      (∀ s, Function.Bijective (fun a : G s ⟶ A ↦ a ≫ g)) → IsIso g) :
    ∀ I : Type v, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) c
